requirements.requirement: Export /srv/nfs/shared from node1 and mount it at /mnt/shared on node2.
requirements.summary: node1 actively exports the requested path exclusively to node2, and node2 shows it mounted read-write as NFSv4 at the requested mount point. The mount and export recovered after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Provide the dataops identity with UID and GID 4500 on both systems.
requirements.summary: Both nodes directly report dataops with UID 4500 and primary GID 4500, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Set the shared directory to dataops:dataops with mode 2770.
requirements.summary: The exported directory and its mounted view consistently report dataops:dataops, numeric ownership 4500:4500, and mode 2770 before and after restarts.

requirements.requirement: Files created from either system retain consistent ownership and permissions across the share.
requirements.summary: Files created as dataops from node1 and node2 were visible from both systems as dataops:dataops (4500:4500) with mode 664. Additional writes after each restart retained the same ownership and mode and were visible on node1.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct end-state and behavioral evidence. The independent restart protocol is also complete for both managed nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity confirmed by commands and lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, mount, identities, permissions, data, and cross-node writes.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, identity and directory creation, export/fstab updates, service activation, test-file creation, and restarts all had clear roles in implementing or verifying the requested outcome and mandatory restart protocol. The bounded temporary configuration and reboot-log files were absent from the post-executor /tmp inventories. Both nodes ended with healthy package state and no failed services; the new NFS/RPC listeners are attributable to the required share, whose export is restricted to node2.
